e2233e47d6df1a46625fae8637d707e866ee08a1: Kitzbüheler Horn is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 17 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Kitzbüheler Horn's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Kitzbüheler Horn's altitude (770 m at the base, 2000 m at the top) helps it keep a decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Kitzbüheler Horn is clearly high: €54 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short: Kitzbüheler Horn does not rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

e29b0a21c54167628293b63e645bb8a6f2e39255: Chamonix offers 110 km of well-marked runs, an intermediate-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 43 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Technical terrain reigns supreme in Chamonix: with 16 black and 44 red runs on offer, confirmed skiers will find plenty to challenge them seriously. Off-piste and freeride are practised here in often excellent conditions, thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. As for snow reliability, Chamonix is in a strong position with its highest point at 3,842m: even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 1,035m is also well placed to guarantee comfortable conditions from mid-December onwards. The budget for a stay in Chamonix is clearly high: 77€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you need to be aware of it before you go. In short: Chamonix keeps its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
